results.title: FigCraft guide, the free Figma alternative written in Rust
results.content:
FigCraft is a free Figma alternative, open source and written in Rust, for designing interfaces and prototypes offline on macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD and in the browser. The official repository went up on October 9, 2026 and counts 2,558 GitHub stars as of October 18. The project calls itself alpha. Drawing screens with components and auto layout already works; properly opening the .fig files that arrive from a client does not, not yet.

Update, 25 October 2026

Update, 23 October 2026

Update, 18 October 2026

FigCraft, a free Figma alternative in Rust, with three screens of a mobile app on the canvas, the layers panel on the left and the Design panel with auto layout on the right [...] Figma, for anyone who doesn't use it, is the reference program for interface design (UI, meaning the screens, buttons and menus of an app or a site; the difference from UX is explained in the guide to UX and UI). The Starter plan is free but limited, while the Professional plan costs $16 a month per full seat, rising to $55 on the Organization plan and $90 on Enterprise, according to the official price list. FigCraft costs nothing, asks for no account, sends no telemetry, saves work to .figcraft archives on disk. The license is dual (MIT or Apache-2.0, take your pick) and allows commercial use. [...] The project presents itself as a clean-room reimplementation, meaning one written without reading the code of the product being imitated. The parity document with Figma describes the method with unusual precision. The authors installed Figma 126.10.7 for macOS and looked only at names, behaviors, public pages and documentation, without ever opening the app's code. At the bottom of the README sits the customary disclaimer, with Figma a trademark of Figma Inc. and FigCraft an independent project, neither affiliated with nor endorsed by the San Francisco company.
